summary_paragraph: A 60-year-old woman with a history of coronary artery disease, diabetes, hypertension, and hyperlipidemia was admitted for substernal chest pain radiating to the left arm and back, triggered by a stressful argument with her son. The pain resolved with nitroglycerin and morphine. Evaluation showed no acute ischemic changes on EKG and normal cardiac enzymes, indicating no myocardial infarction. Her symptoms were consistent with prior stress-related episodes. She was hypoglycemic on arrival (glucose 43), which resolved, but her HbA1c was elevated at 10.0, reflecting poor long-term diabetes control. Triglycerides were markedly elevated, though not fasting. Social work addressed her concerns about verbal and physical abuse from her son; she elected to stay with her boyfriend and pursue a restraining order. She remained stable, with no recurrence of chest pain, and was discharged home with continued cardiac and diabetes medications and follow-up plans.
